newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: TWO FIRMS CHALLENGE RULING IN ARGENTINE POST SALE.
newsitem.headline: TWO FIRMS CHALLENGE RULING IN ARGENTINE POST SALE.

text.p: A Dutch group headed by ING Barings and local building firm Roggio said Monday they will challenge an official ruling that they did not qualify to bid for the concession to run Argentine postal firm ENCOTESA.
"Our decision is to challenge," ING Barings Argentina President Steven Darch told Reuters.
"A negative answer ... would be absolutely incoherent and in case it is negative we obviously would have to take the case to the courts."
ING Bank NV-Cayman Islands Funds N.V plans to protest the ruling to the commission handling the awarding of ENCOTESA's concession before the Wednesday deadline, Darch said.
Separately, Juan Bautista Ordonez, communications manager for building firm Roggio, said it would follow suit.
"We will challenge the decision Tuesday, especially the point ... that deals with the status of our postal operator."
Asked whether they would also go to courts in case their challenge to the commission is rejected, he said "that would be up to the response. We have no scenarios for not qualifying."
ING and Roggio are two of three groups or firms --over a total of six bidders-- that the commission said did not qualify for ENCOTESA's 30-year concession.
Arturo Puricelli, ENCOTESA's president, said last week the Dutch group and Roggio's proposed postal operators were not affiliated to the Universal Postal Union (UPU) as required.

ING took Nepostel Consultancy NV as postal operator while Roggio took Canada Post System Management Ltd (CPSM). Puricelli said Nepostel and CPSM are merely consultants belonging respectively to the Dutch and Canadian state postal firms, but not official post companies themselves.
But the UPU has told ENCOTESA that both Nepostel and CSPM should be considered integral part of the official postal services of the Netherlands and Canada, respectively.

A Brazilian headed group was left out of race on the grounds that it failed to present an investment plan, said it was considering a challenge to the decision. It had proposed Italy's post office as operator.
"We are in talks with our lawyers about a possible challenge," Jose Chalen, representative of the group headed by Brazilian airline VASP .
"We included an investment plan in the body our presentation. Only that it was not identified as such, and then we get into subjective ground."
Challengers must deposit $500,000 which would be reimbursed in case the challenge is accepted.
Three other groups qualified for ENCOTESA's:
- Local transport company TAC, local group Roman and businessman Samuel Liberman, owner of local cable TV firm VCC, with Germany's state post office as operator; -- Itron and
Sideco --controlled by local holding company Grupo Macri-- and local Banco de Galicia , with the British Post Office; -- Local banking group Werthein and COINTEL, a holding

which controls Telefonica de Argentina , and New Zealand's Infratil International with New Zealand Post. COINTEL is jointly owned by Telefonica de Espana and local CEI Citicorp Holding SA , which is about 40 percent indirectly owned by Citibank .
The result of the bidding will be announced July 28.
((--Buenos Aies Newsroom, 541 318-0650))
